IWC tables of estimates of abundances

gmd:abstract.gco:CharacterString: Whales play a critical role in marine ecosystems, yet their conservation and management require accurate and accessible global abundance and distribution data. This is a high-resolution dataset of whale abundance estimates, compiled from diverse sources, including systematic surveys, ecological models, and historical records. Each record is linked to spatial polygons representing the presumed area of occupancy, forming a geodatabase that facilitates spatially explicit analyses. The aim of the tables of Accepted Abundance Estimates is (i) to collate information in a consistent way on abundance estimates accepted by the Scientific Committee for various purposes and (ii) to provide a simplified table of abundance estimates suitable as a broad overview for the Commission and the public. See IWC 2014 (JCRM 15 suppl. p416-7) for further details on the objectives. The dataset originated from efforts to support stock assessments for the International Whaling Commission (IWC). Initially an ad hoc compilation, the dataset evolved through the formal review process developed by the IWC Scientific Committee’s Sub-Committee on Abundance Estimates, Stock Status, and International Databases (ASI). The dataset has since been restructured and enhanced to include a spatial component, enabling advanced visualisation and integration with spatial management tools. While not yet comprehensive, this dataset is designed to be a live resource, updated with new abundance estimates as they become available. An RShiny application has also been developed to enhance accessibility, allowing users to visualise and explore the data interactively. This dataset provides a valuable resource for researchers, conservation practitioners, and policymakers. It supports ecological modelling, habitat use studies, and marine management strategies. It offers a foundation for addressing key questions in marine biodiversity conservation, assessing anthropogenic impacts, and informing international efforts to protect whale populations under changing environmental conditions.

gmd:statement.gco:CharacterString: The IWC Abundance Tables serve as a centralised repository for whale abundance estimates and a comprehensive resource designed to consolidate evaluated whale abundance estimates, supporting the work of the IWC Scientific Committee (SC). The collation process involves the systematic collection and documentation of abundance estimates, along with related information and review outcomes, ensuring that the data are standardised, traceable, and fit for scientific and management purposes. Sampling Description: The data collation process involves gathering abundance estimates submitted through working papers or external documents to the IWC SC, standardising their accompanying metadata, and incorporating the outcomes of rigorous review processes conducted by the Abundance Steering Group (ASG) and Sub-committee on Abundance Estimates, Stock Status, and International Cruises (ASI) groups. The collation ensures that all abundance estimates are traceable and their traits are organised by adhering to a transparent and consistent process.
